subject: VPC scoping & data-sovereignty gatekeeper asks — post-discovery
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>
To: Kelly Ramos <kelly@mediscope.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: VPC scoping & data sovereignty — key asks from today

Kelly — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Below is a concise playback of what we heard plus the immediate asks from Redwood to keep the evaluation moving. Please correct anything we misinterpreted.

Summary of pain and goals
- Pain: current vendor latency/cost and lack of predictable isolation for PHI workloads.
- Regulatory goal: All PHI and derived inference logs must remain in US-controlled infrastructure; no cross-border backups or analytics without explicit consent and contractual restrictions.
- Ops constraint: Primary inference must run inside a customer-managed VPC with restricted outbound egress (approved proxy/NAT only).

Technical constraints called out
- No direct public egress from model hosts; egress allowed only to an approved proxy/NAT with TLS inspection disabled for PHI flows.
- We need support for bringing your KMS (AWS KMS customer-managed key) or integration with HSM-backed key service.
- Optional: an air-gapped enclave for model fine-tuning or evaluation — Mediscope may later require airgap for experimental datasets, but not required for initial pilot.

Immediate asks from Redwood (what we need to proceed)
1) Confirmation of data residency boundaries: one-line confirmation that all PHI for this project must stay within US regions (yes/no + any state-level caveats).
2) Network restrictions doc: short list of allowed outbound CIDR / proxy FQDNs and whether 443 outbound is allowed only via approved NAT.
3) SOC2 / ISO evidence: if you can share an internal compliance inventory or SOC2 snapshot for the environment currently hosting medapps (we understand this is sensitive — a stub is fine).
4) Tech deep-dive availability: propose Wed 2026-11-18 10:00 PT for a 60m session with our runtime and networking architects.

What Redwood will deliver next
- A draft mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and owners (skeleton attached: MAP_v1.xlsx).
- A templated VPC diagram with recommended firewall/NAT placement for our private deployment path (attached: naomi_vpc_template_v1.drawio.png).
- A short SOC2 evidence checklist mapping items we typically need for private deployments.

If that aligns, please send the network allowlist and confirm the residency statement. I can schedule the tech deep-dive once you confirm availability.

Attachments referenced: MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan skeleton), naomi_vpc_template_v1.drawio.png (redwood recommended layout), SOC2_snapshot.pdf (redacted example of what we request).

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.example
+1 (415) 555-0127

From: Kelly Ramos <kelly@mediscope.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>
Cc: Mediscope Security <security@mediscope.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC scoping & data sovereignty — key asks from today

Naomi — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- Residency: Confirmed — all PHI and generated inference logs must remain in US regions. No cross-border analytics without an executed DPA addendum.
- Network: We operate behind an approved egress proxy; outbound to public internet is allowed only through that proxy/NAT. We will need Redwood to limit its outbound endpoints to a small allowlist (we'll provide CIDR/FQDNs).
- Airgap: We likely will NOT require a full air-gapped model training environment for the pilot. We may revisit for R&D later.

I've attached our compliance inventory workbook that lists current attestations and contact points. We'll circulate the network allowlist and a short procurement checklist by EOD Friday.

Attaching: mediscope_compliance_inventory.xlsx (sensitive)

Kelly Ramos
Head of IT Operations | Mediscope
kelly@mediscope.com
+1 (212) 555-0199

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC scoping & data sovereignty — key asks from today

Kelly — appreciated. A few notes on Redwood's side and suggested owners/timing: 
- Owner: I'll drive the pilot SOW and procurement checklist; Markus will own the runtime configuration and KMS/HSM integration work. Naomi will run the tech deep-dive.
- Evidence: The compliance workbook you attached looks good for initial triage; for the security review we'll need the specific SOC2 sections related to system configuration and change control (a redacted PDF is fine).
- Network: once you share the allowlist we will do an internal validation and provide a minimal set of IPs/FQDNs your proxy needs to allow (expect a shortlist within 48 hours of receiving your list).

Next steps we propose: 
1) Kelly to send allowlist + any procurement gating documents by EOD Fri (2026-11-13).
2) Naomi to lock tech deep-dive (Wed 11/18 10:00 PT).
3) Ben to share initial SOW checklist and expected commercial timing (target: draft by 11/20).

Attaching: SOW_checklist_stub.pdf (internal).

Thanks — we'll keep this tight to avoid procurement stalls.

Ben Carter
